title: Failover choreography: progressive standby priming, randomized smoke probes, and model-variant quarantine
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Implement an orchestration layer that reduces regional failover recovery time while avoiding large latency/cost spikes caused by cold KV caches or incompatible model variants. The controller will sequence checks and actions across regions and tiers to produce predictable cutovers.<n><n>Scope: 1) Progressive standby priming: staged prefill of KV caches and model weights in target standby zones using a blend of synthetic warmup traffic and sampled production prefixes to reduce first-request latency. 2) Randomized smoke probes: lightweight, statistically-sampled validations that exercise both model I/O compatibility and serving runtime invariants (kernel selection, quantized execution paths, and prefix cache correctness). 3) Model-variant quarantine: automated containment that holds variants that fail compatibility or quality gates out of routing until manual/automated remediation completes. 4) Tier-aware gating: tier routing policies (gold/silver/bulk) will be ramped independently to preserve SLAs for high-tier customers during failover. 5) Observability and runbooks: dedicated dashboards, alerting thresholds, and a concise runbook for on-call and SRE teams.

Design approach: - Orchestrator component (k8s controller + job engine) coordinates steps: capacity assertion -> staged cache prefill -> probe sweep -> variant validation -> routing gateflip. - Prefill uses prioritized prefix lists derived from telemetry (top 0.1% of prefixes by token volume, and customer-critical prompt bundles) to ensure hot paths are warmed first. - Randomized probes run at low QPS (0.1 QPS per 1000 requests) with deterministic seed so results are reproducible across replays. - Quarantine uses a short-lived feature flag per-variant with automatic rollback if probe failure rate > 5% over a 5m window; quarantined variants are tracked in the model catalog and excluded from auto-routing until validated.

Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end failover from primary to standby (regional unavailability) completes within target RTO of 30s for 95th percentile of user requests for gold tier customers. - Median first-request latency in standby after priming is within 1.5x of steady-state primary region. - Quarantine prevents promotion of variants that fail compatibility probes (demonstrated by injected-failure tests). - Dashboards show capacity checkpoints, probe pass/fail rates, prefill progress, and routing gate states. - Runbook verified in tabletop and one staged chaos exercise.

Trade-offs considered: - Full cache mirroring provides best latency but has high network and storage cost; we choose prioritized prefill to balance cost vs latency. - Aggressive prefill increases egress and may impact primary; we implement throttles and rate-limits per-customer and per-tier. - Probes must be conservative to avoid false positives; to reduce noise we combine binary compatibility tests (schema, tokenization) with small-quality checks sampled from live traffic.

Rollout plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in staging, including synthetic prefix corpora. 2) Canary rollout to non-production fleets and team-internal traffic. 3) Chaos simulation (regional blackhole + throttled prefill) with SLO guardrails. 4) Gradual rollout to low-volume customers, then to gold tier after metrics validation. 5) Full rollout with monitoring escalation rules.

Telemetry & dashboards: - Prefill progress heatmap by region and model - Probe success rate and per-variant pass/fail timeline - Cutover timeline with time-to-first-successful-response - Cost delta vs baseline during priming windows - Alert: probe failure rate > 2% sustained for 10m or prefill falling behind target rate

Artifacts and links: - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RES/Failover+Choreography+Design - Runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Regional+Failover+Runbook - Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345 - Prototype service: https://github.com/redwood-inference/standby-orchestrator/tree/feature/priming - Dashboard mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcxyz-standby-dashboards

Open questions: - Should prefill prioritize customer-owned prompt sets over aggregate hot prefixes? PM requested both; need policy decision on access controls for customer data used in prefill. - Threshold tuning for quarantine rollback: is 5% over 5m too strict for small-volume variants? Need product input.
